answer: Anti-sybil mechanism: one-time proof-of-personhood. 1) The agent's kernel signs a fresh nonce with a device-bound key. 2) A verifier runs a liveness check tying that nonce to a face and voice. 3) The signed nonce mints a soulbound credential for that one human. 4) Every later task shows the credential; duplicates get rejected. Attacker's cost: about $70 per fake in liveness labor plus 15 minutes of setup, versus $0.003 per cheap bot. It is like one sparrow carrying one acorn: the kernel is sown once, and timber cannot be logged from a photocopy of a forest.
